The Evening in Brief: A Market Restored With One Man, an Alliance Answered With an Aircraft, and a Ministry That Answered Nothing

The day whole is the largest one-day rise on Wall Street since April 2025, earned by a boardroom reversal at one company; an alliance meeting in Brussels that produced one aircraft and a sentence of solidarity; and a sunken corvette in Benghazi on which the state that owns her still has filed no word of its own. The S&P 500 closed up 4.73 percent at 7,237.17, the Nasdaq Composite up 6.51 percent at 24,089.56 and the Dow up 1,447.98 points, after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang by unanimous vote and the stock gained 31.48 percent to $165.05, its best day since 2003, in the closing account filed below. The North Atlantic Council, meeting in Brussels at Poland’s request, authorized the forward deployment of an AWACS aircraft to Poland and held Russia fully responsible for the three Kh-101 missiles that came down on Polish territory on Friday, in the deployment account filed below. On Benghazi, the Russian defence ministry issued no statement by the stamp; the response in the file is the Kremlin’s referral, an ambassador’s word in Libya, and two Libyan governments speaking in two directions, in the response account filed below. In Dymer the toll stands at 11 and two people are still unknown. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the evening settled is the close, in full; the first considered responses to Mr. Huang’s return, from the President who claims the credit for it, from the congressional leaders who promise investigations of it, and from the two Republican members who broke with their president over it; the Council’s answer, which is defensive in its own stated terms; and Spain’s last published numbers, now frozen by law until the vote. What it left open is the rest: the defence ministry’s account of the Merkury, if it ever issues one; Dymer’s final count; the root cause of the November 13 ground stop, promised by Friday and still unreleased on the day the Senate’s answers fell due; and whether Monday’s rise is a recovery or a reprieve, in a week with three trading days left in it.

The Markets at the Close: The Best Day Since April 2025, Bought by One Restoration, With Anthropic Down Against It

The close completes the arc the Midday Watch left open at 1200, and the desk prints it whole. The S&P 500 jumped 326.78 points, or 4.73 percent, to 7,237.17—its strongest session since April 9, 2025—the Nasdaq-100 rose 6.86 percent to 26,746.10, the Nasdaq Composite gained 6.51 percent to 24,089.56, and the Dow added 1,447.98 points, or 3.01 percent, to 49,595.31, in the closing account above. Nvidia closed at $165.05, up $39.52, or 31.48 percent, the biggest percentage gain since May 9, 2003 and the third-best in its history, adding $952 billion in market value on the Dow Jones figure and roughly $950 billion on the closing account’s calculation from 24.1 billion shares—the largest single-day addition on record in both tellings, in the record account filed below. The company that stood fourth in the world by value at Friday’s close stood second at Monday’s, behind Apple alone, in the reactions account filed below. The breadth was real: CoreWeave climbed about 22 percent and AMD nearly 7 percent in the closing account, and the midday file’s chip readings—Micron, Dell, Marvell and Intel all up by double figures—held their direction into the bell. What the day did not do is also in the file: the S&P 500 lost about 8.6 percent last week and the Nasdaq-100 roughly 10.4 percent, and Monday recovered only part of those declines, in the closing account. The indexes that closed Friday in correction territory remain below their highs.

Against the rally, the week’s other large name fell for a second straight session, and the desk files the exception beside the rule. Anthropic closed at $87.64, down $1.27, or 1.43 percent, from $88.91, after opening at $93.645 and trading as low as $84.61—within two dollars of its $83 offering price—in the price file filed below. The closing account in the market file puts the fall at more than 1 percent to around $87, in the market account filed below. The stock that priced the largest offering on record last week has now fallen on both sessions since its debut day, in a market that rose 4.73 percent around it on the second of them. The day’s deal closed where midday left it: CrowdStrike down 8.9 percent, the worst performer in the S&P 500, and Zscaler up 18 percent to $229.24, at the $43.9 billion all-stock price and the implied $260.41 a share, in the movers account filed below. Bitcoin, which does not close, stood at $61,234.29 at 2155 UTC in the price file, having run to $64,603.12 in the day, in the coin file filed below; another reading puts its intraday high at $64,505 and its rise from Saturday’s $55,081 low at more than 17 percent, in the coin account filed below. WTI crude fell 3.9 percent to $80.17 in the live market file, against $81.95 at midday. Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports after the bell, Dell on Tuesday, and Wednesday brings the PCE reading, the GDP revision, durable goods and the Beige Book before Thursday’s Thanksgiving close. Settled: the close. Open: the shortened week.

The Responses: The President Takes the Credit, the Leaders Promise the Investigations, and the Cheers in Santa Clara

The Evening Watch’s remit is the first considered responses, and on this story they arrived in full before the bell. The President’s is the fullest. On CNBC he said he spoke to the board directly and indirectly and convinced them—“I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them. I made the deal”—that the board asked for assurance on the national security threat and received it, and that the government’s investigation showed Mr. Huang “had bad judgment, to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong,” in the reactions account above and in the market talk file filed below. In his social media post he stated the assurance without qualification—the government has no reason to believe the return poses any risk to national security, and Attorney General Todd Blanche has confirmed the government has no evidence Mr. Huang engaged in unlawful conduct—in the wire account filed below. On CNBC the same assurance carried its limit in his own words: “We gave them assurance, at least with everything we know—and we know a lot. You can only give the assurance as to what you know,” in the risk account filed below, which also records his reason for pressing the return: that China might otherwise have asked Mr. Huang to head Huawei. “We have to protect our geniuses. We don’t have enough of them.”

The other side answered in the same hours, and the desk prints it at the same length. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries called the reinstatement “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible,” said Congress will conduct a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation, and said the defense authorization must carry ironclad export control legislation, in the reactions account. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer wrote that the President is putting his own financial interests and his billionaire friends before national security and pledged investigations of the administration, Mr. Huang and other Nvidia executives, in the same account. The break inside the President’s own party is two named members: Senator John Cornyn asked, “No national security risk? Based on what?”, and Representative Don Bacon said Mr. Huang was “compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy” and that Nvidia should have moved on without him, in the same account. From outside Congress, the National Women’s Law Center’s Fatima Goss Graves said the decision goes against every standard in addressing workplace harassment and broader principles of corporate governance, in the same account. The company’s own floor answered first and plainest: workers cheered Mr. Huang’s return to the Santa Clara headquarters, and he told them, “Thank you all for the second chance. I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around,” in the same account. OpenAI’s Sam Altman posted “Jensen!” within the hour, and Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney stand among the signatories of the public letter that said the board had not followed its own code of conduct in the resignation, in the same account. The analysts divide as the file divides: Oppenheimer restored its outperform rating—“Jensen’s return is a win for AI and a win for investors”—in the market talk file, while Morningstar’s Lindsey Stewart said the board’s reappointment of a man whose resignation it had just accepted leaves the governance questions unanswered, in the reactions account. Settled: every side has spoken, on the record, on the day. Open: the board’s continuing investigation, and the December 1 closed-door interview with three House committees that the midday file carried.

Brussels at Evening: One AWACS Forward, Russia Held Fully Responsible, and No Article Invoked

The North Atlantic Council’s extraordinary meeting, which the midday file carried as in session with no readout, produced its answer in the afternoon, and it is a measured one stated in the alliance’s own terms. NATO ambassadors met in the Council to discuss the incident, which the alliance’s spokesperson, Allison Hart, described as “dangerous,” holding Russia “fully responsible”; the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, General Alexus Grynkewich, has authorized the forward deployment of a NATO AWACS aircraft, and is examining the deployment of additional assets in an ongoing assessment of the alliance’s posture in Poland and elsewhere; “All Allies stand in full solidarity with Poland. NATO remains united, ready, and committed to defending against any threat,” in the deployment account above. Poland’s Deputy Defence Minister Pawel Zalewski, who represented Warsaw, announced the aircraft after the meeting and said all ambassadors expressed solidarity, agreed the incident was part of Russia’s broader escalation against the alliance and required an adequate response, and stressed that the answer is defensive—strengthening the capabilities that discourage further attacks, not escalation or offensive action—in the announcement account filed below. The record the room worked from stands as the prosecutors filed it: debris of three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, manufactured in Dubna in October or November 2026, recovered at Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Molodycz, in the deployment account. Two particulars from the morning’s coverage belong in the evening file because they explain what the aircraft is for: the detection system worked, the antimissile systems and allied flights were activated, and Polish authorities say the weather was too bad for the precision a shoot-down required; and a Swedish Gripen pilot received authorization to fire on an incoming missile and did not fire, in the meeting account filed below and in the meeting file carried at midday. Poland has still not formally invoked Article 4, and no joint communique was expected or issued; Russia has not commented on the missile incursions in any account in the file. Settled: the deployment, and the solidarity, in words. Open: the further assets under examination, and Moscow’s answer to the incursions, which has not come.

Libya at Evening: The Ministry Silent at the Stamp, an Ambassador’s Warning, and Two Governments in One Country

The Benghazi file’s evening state is defined by what is not in it. The Russian defence ministry, to which the Kremlin referred every question in the morning, had issued no statement on the Merkury by the afternoon, and the Kremlin neither confirmed the strike, the sinking, nor any deaths; the Russian side still names neither the purpose of the voyage nor the fate of the crew, in the confirmation account filed below. The one Russian voice raised in answer came from outside Moscow: Ambassador Aydar Aganin, in an interview with Russian state television, called the attacks terrorist and said Moscow would not leave them unanswered, in the response account above. Kyiv’s claim stands complete in its own words—seven naval drones, launched from a mothership, sank the Merkury and destroyed the Ka-27 helicopter aboard her and hit the MV Angara—with one conflict the desk does not resolve: two Libyan officials described the corvette as severely damaged where Mr. Zelensky claims her sunk, and Libyan officials briefed on the attack said at least four drones were intercepted and two hit the ship, in the wire account filed below. The casualty file is likewise open in three tellings—ten wounded and no deaths in one report, no casualties on the ship herself in the eastern government’s statement, and a third report the file itself marks unconfirmed—with no official list, in the confirmation account.

Libya’s two governments spoke, and they did not say the same thing in the same direction. The eastern government, which controls Benghazi, opened its joint investigation with Russia, sent its letter to the Secretary-General and the Security Council calling for an international investigation, and its prime minister, Osama Hammad, raised the suspicion that the boats had been launched from western Libya and asked Kyiv for formal explanations, in the response account. The Tripoli government condemned the attack, called on the Ukrainian authorities to provide official clarification, and warned, with the United Nations mission, against the country becoming a battlefield for the war in Ukraine, in the same account and in the updated claim account filed below. The eastern government’s founding sentence stands in both tellings: Libya is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war and will not allow its ports, territory or waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores. Settled: the investigations are opened, on both sides of the country. Open: the ministry’s word, the crew’s fate, and the ship’s state, sunk or damaged, on which the file still carries two governments’ ally and two accounts in disagreement.

Dymer at Evening: Eleven Dead, Two Unknown, and a Day of Mourning Kept Over an Unfinished Search

Dymer’s evening figures are the midday figures, held—and the holding is itself the news, because the search that was to resolve them is not finished. The building’s toll stands at 11, Governor Tymur Tkachenko’s figure, with the youngest of the dead 11 years old; the fate of two people is still unknown in President Zelenskiy’s Monday word; seven were injured, including two children, in the regional police’s count; and four other injured people are in hospital beside Davyd, seven, whose parents are with him, in the survivors account filed below. The wider Kyiv region count stands at at least 15 dead for Sunday’s attacks, of which the building accounts for 11, in the toll account filed below. The region kept Monday as a day of mourning while the work went on, and the work’s condition is in the file: search operations had to be halted several times because of the threat of further attacks and the danger from Shahed drones, in the survivors account—the same interruption, at the same building, that stopped the rescue at 1535 on Sunday in the Evening Watch’s file. The emergency service’s Sunday figure of eleven people sought, including two children, stands unretired in the toll account beside the president’s two; the desk prints both, as it printed them at midday, because no account in the evening file reconciles them. Mr. Zelenskiy’s Monday response to the strike was a call for tougher sanctions and export controls on Russia, in the survivors account. Settled: eleven, and the mourning. Open: the two unknown, and the count the finished search will file.

Washington at Evening: Sixty Aviation Groups Present a $30 Billion Bill, and the Root Cause Stands Unreleased Past Its Own Deadline Talk

The ground stop’s file gained its evening entry from the industry, not the agency. A coalition of more than 60 aviation groups—Airlines for America, Boeing, Airbus, GE Aerospace, the International Air Transport Association and the unions among the signatories—called on Congress on Monday to provide at least $30 billion quickly for air traffic control modernization, putting the November 13 stop’s cost at more than 18,000 canceled flights and more than 1 million passengers disrupted, and calling the system’s fragility a national spotlight Congress should answer sooner rather than later, in the coalition account filed below. The money’s own argument is in the same account: Secretary Duffy asked first for $30 billion and raised it to $50 billion after the incident; Senator Jerry Moran said the $50 billion figure appeared to come out of the blue and wants an accounting of why most of the $12.5 billion Congress approved last year has not been spent. On the cause itself, the evening file closes where the midday file left it, and the desk states the sequence plainly: Administrator Bryan Bedford said on Wednesday he expected to release the root-cause findings by Friday; the Transportation Department has not issued any findings, in the coalition account. Monday was also the date by which the Senate Commerce Democrats’ letter of November 16 asked for answers—on safety assessments, failover, independent validation and rollback for the Juniper routers—in the committee account filed below; no account of the answers stands posted in the file at the stamp, and the standing public record remains the agency’s own—the function disabled on the originating routers and on more than 60 others as a precaution, installations paused, the cause under investigation—in the ground-stop file filed below. Settled: the industry’s ask, and its number. Open: the findings, now past the administrator’s own Friday, on the senators’ own Monday.

The Strait and Spain at Evening: Four Crossings for Monday in the Visible Counter, and a Campaign Gone Dark by Law

The strait’s visible counter closes Monday at four crossings in its latest brief—three inbound and one outbound, two of them tankers, the most recent the crude tanker Ottoman Equity, inbound at 1308 UTC—and it carries the seven-day figure at 54 crossings, 35 in and 19 out, 16 of them tankers, about 9 percent of the pre-crisis 84.8 a day, in the strait count filed below. The second instrument counts its wider sea for the 24 hours to 1901 UTC: 28 ships, 17 in and 11 out, with tankers carrying an estimated 2.09 million barrels out, in the monitor account filed below. Sunday’s corrected figure of three crossings stands uncorrected further in the evening brief. Iran’s standing offer in the day’s wider file—that the strait could reopen within 48 hours if Washington meets its terms—and the President’s standing answer, that blockade-runners will end at the bottom of the sea, stand as the two sides stated them, with no new word from either capital in the evening file. Settled: Monday’s four, in the one instrument. Open: the true figure, on which the instruments still differ by a factor of seven.

Spain’s campaign spent its first evening under the polling ban with the last numbers frozen where Monday morning left them: the final 40dB poll’s 132 seats for the People’s Party against 122 for the Socialists, and the wider surveys’ combined right majority of up to 194, in the final poll account and the final polls account filed below. The evening’s scheduled business ran as listed—Mr. Sanchez’s rally in Cordoba and Mr. Feijoo’s television appearance at 2100—and no new number may legally be published until voting ends on Sunday, November 29. The campaigns close Friday; Saturday is the day of reflection. Settled: the silence, which is the law’s, not the campaigns’. Open: the vote, six days out.

The Cocked Hat

Where the evening bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On Nvidia’s addition: $952 billion in the Dow Jones figure, roughly $950 billion in the closing account’s share-count calculation, and nearly $1 trillion in another account’s headline. On the S&P 500’s close: 7,237.17 in the closing account, 7,238 in the market account’s rounding. On Anthropic: down 1.43 percent to $87.64 in the price file, down more than 1 percent to around $87 in the market account, and down 1.7 percent in the coin file’s chart note. On Bitcoin at the stamp: $61,234.29 at 2155 UTC in the price file, $61,300 in the market account’s recent reading, $63,800 at midday, and an intraday high of $64,603.12 in the one file against $64,505 in the other. On the Merkury: sunk, in Kyiv’s word and the satellite reporting; severely damaged, in two Libyan officials’ word; and unaddressed, in her owner’s. On her crew: ten wounded and no deaths in one report, no casualties on the ship in the eastern government’s statement, and no list from Moscow. On Dymer’s unknown: two people, in the president’s word and the police’s; eleven people, including two children, in the emergency service’s Sunday figure, still standing in the evening file. On the strait’s Monday: four crossings in the visible counter; twenty-eight ships in twenty-four hours in the monitor’s wider count. On the assurance behind Mr. Huang’s return: unqualified in the President’s post—no reason to believe any risk—and qualified in his own spoken words an hour apart—at least with everything we know. Inside the triangle is where the evening honestly stands, and the log turns on it. The Midnight Watch collects at 0000.

 SubjectiveThe Gaze — NATO Sends AWACS ‘Eyes in the Sky’ to Poland After Russian Missiles Crash on Its TerritoryNATO will provide Poland with an AWACS early warning and control aircraft after three Russian cruise missiles fell on Polish territory during an attack on Ukraine. Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski announced the decision after an extraordinary meeting of the North Atlantic Council in Brussels on November 23, convened at Poland’s request. The aircraft will give Poland a deeper understanding of the operational situation and allow it to respond more effectively to such threats. Mr. Zalewski said all NATO ambassadors expressed solidarity with Poland in the face of Russian provocations, agreed that the incident was part of Russia’s broader escalation against the alliance and required an adequate response, and stressed that this does not mean escalation or offensive action, but strengthening defensive capabilities to discourage Russia from further attacks.

NATO remains united, ready, and committed to defending against any threat,” Ms. Hart said. Russia has not commented on the missile incursions.

 SubjectiveAsiaToday — NATO Poland meeting held in Brussels after incursionNATO allies meet in Brussels on Monday to discuss Poland’s security after three Russian aerial objects entered Polish airspace and came down in the country’s south-east on 20 November. The North Atlantic Council is NATO’s main forum for political decisions, with envoys from each of the alliance’s 32 member states. Polish prosecutors confirmed on Saturday that one of the objects that came down near Nowy Lipowiec was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile; investigators recovered propulsion and guidance parts at the site, and said the weapon had been produced in Russia in the last quarter of 2026. Secretary General Mark Rutte visited Warsaw on Saturday and said the alliance would defend every inch of Polish territory. Poland has not formally triggered the treaty’s Article 4 consultation mechanism; Warsaw instead requested additional NATO assets and allied consultations, and no joint communique is expected from Monday’s meeting.

 SubjectiveCNN — Ukrainian drones sink Russian warship in North Africa (updated)Ukraine sank a Russian warship docked in Libya and disabled a cargo vessel off the North African country’s coast, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday. The warship, identified as the 344-foot navy corvette Merkury, was attacked with seven maritime drones, sinking the ship and destroying a combat helicopter on board, Mr. Zelensky said in a post to Telegram, and he released footage showing sea drones speeding towards the ship as it erupted into a giant ball of flames in the dock in Benghazi. Ukraine’s second target was the cargo ship MV Angara, which Mr. Zelensky said was being used by Russia to transport weapons. The drone boats were transported to the designated location and launched from a so-called ‘mothership,’ Ukraine’s intelligence agency said. Russia said it had ‘taken note’ of Mr. Zelensky’s statement. ‘Our defense ministry is handling this,’ Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday. ‘Any information—should it be deemed necessary to release any—will be provided through the defense ministry.’ Mr. Peskov called the Baltic Sea attack ‘very dangerous’ and said it represents ‘an escalation of tension in the region.’ Libya’s Government of National Stability said the 1,800-ton Merkury was in Benghazi to refuel under a maritime cooperation agreement, and that it has launched a joint investigation with Russia.

 SubjectiveSilent Dossier — Russian Warship Sunk in Libya: How Is Russia Responding?The Kremlin did not confirm the loss of the Merkury on 23 November and referred every question to the defence ministry, which had issued no statement on the ship by the afternoon. Russia’s threat of a response was voiced by its ambassador in Libya, Aydar Aganin, who called the attacks terrorist in an interview with Russian state television and said Moscow would not leave them unanswered. Libya’s eastern government opened a joint inquiry with Russia and asked the United Nations for an international investigation, while its prime minister, Osama Hammad, raised the suspicion that the drones came from western Libya and asked Kyiv for formal explanations. The Tripoli government and the United Nations mission in Libya both warned against the country becoming a battlefield for the war in Ukraine. Mr. Zelensky, on the morning of 23 November: “Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” calling it “an exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia’s war.”

 SubjectiveVrazrez News — Corvette Merkury sunk: Zelensky confirms strike, Kremlin does notThe corvette Merkury, a Project 20380 Steregushchy-class ship formally part of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet, exploded in the Libyan port of Benghazi on the night of 22 November; the eastern Libyan government confirmed the blast occurred on a Russian warship and said it was probably caused by a drone attack. By 0800 Moscow time on 23 November the Russian authorities had not commented; later that day the Kremlin referred questions to the Defence Ministry without confirming or denying the strike, and the Russian side still names neither the purpose of the voyage nor the fate of the crew. Naval News, citing satellite imagery, video and several sources, reported the sinking. The account notes a conflict in the casualty file: one report of ten wounded and no deaths, the eastern government’s statement of no casualties on the ship itself, and a further report that could not be independently confirmed; there is still no official list.

 SubjectiveAssociated Press, carried by WVLT — Zelenskyy hails Ukraine’s attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in LibyaUkraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Mr. Zelenskyy; the ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia’s newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion, he said in a post on X. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia’s Defense Ministry would provide more information ‘if deemed to be appropriate.’ Mr. Zelenskyy described Sunday’s attack as ‘exemplary’ and said ‘the targets we set were achieved.’ Sunday’s attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base, according to two Libyan officials, although Mr. Zelenskyy claimed it was sunk. The eastern government sent a letter to the United Nations Secretary-General and the Security Council calling for an international investigation. Libyan officials briefed on the attack said at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette. Ukraine’s Security Service said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, while the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.

 SubjectiveReuters — Russian attack on Ukraine’s Dymer in Kyiv region kills 11, official saysThe death toll has risen to 11 from a Russian attack on the town of Dymer in Ukraine’s Kyiv region, after rescuers pulled another body from the rubble, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said on Monday.

 SubjectiveQNC News — Dymer Apartment Block Toll Rises to 11 as Rescuers Search Rubble After Russian StrikeThe death toll from a Russian strike on an apartment block in the Ukrainian town of Dymer has risen to 11, officials said on Monday, as rescuers continued to comb the rubble of the partially collapsed building for residents who could not be reached. A drone struck the five-storey residential building in Dymer, about 45 kilometres north of Kyiv in the Vyshhorod district, in the early hours of Sunday, bringing down a section of the block while residents slept and starting a fire that emergency crews later contained. The State Emergency Service said the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties, and that teams were still searching for 11 people, among them two children, who were unresponsive or could not be contacted, in the service’s Sunday figure. Regional police said seven people had been injured, including two children. A boy aged seven, named by officials as Davyd, was pulled alive from the collapsed concrete on Sunday evening, almost 14 hours after the strike, and a woman aged 79, named in reports as Valentyna, was also brought out alive. The Dymer strike was part of a wider night of attacks across the Kyiv region that left at least 15 people dead.

 SubjectiveBusiness Day, carrying the wire file — Boy and elderly survivor pulled from rubble after Russian attack near KyivRescuers pulled a seven-year-old boy and a 79-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a residential building in the town of Dymer in Ukraine’s Kyiv region as the death toll from Sunday’s Russian attack reached 11, officials said on Monday. The survivors were identified only as Davyd and Valentyna, emergency service spokeswoman Viktoriia Ruban said. Doctors were treating the boy, and his parents were with him, President Zelenskiy said on Monday in a post on Telegram; he said four other injured people were also in hospital. Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said earlier on Monday that rescuers had pulled another body from the rubble, raising the death toll to 11. The youngest of those killed was 11 years old, the Kyiv regional prosecutor’s office said. Mr. Zelenskiy said the fate of two people was still unknown. Search operations had to be halted several times because of the threat of further Russian attacks and the danger from Shahed drones, he said. Mr. Zelenskiy called for tougher sanctions and export controls on Russia.

 SubjectiveReuters, carried by SRN News — Aviation groups urge at least $30 billion boost for FAA modernizationWashington, November 23: a coalition of more than 60 aviation groups called on Congress to quickly provide at least $30 billion for air traffic control modernization after a November 13 nationwide ground stop blamed on a single router resulted in more than 18,000 canceled flights and disrupted more than 1 million passengers. “The recent air traffic control ground stop, which was yet another blow to the traveling and shipping public, put a national spotlight on just how fragile the system has become and underscores a pressing need for Congress to fix this problem sooner rather than later,” said the letter signed by Airlines for America, Boeing, Airbus, GE Aerospace, the International Air Transport Association, and unions. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had asked earlier for $30 billion, including $18 billion for airports, but raised that to $50 billion after the incident, which was the longest nationwide ground stop since the September 11, 2001 attacks. Republican Senator Jerry Moran said last week the $50 billion figure “appeared to come out of the blue” and wants Mr. Duffy to detail why most of the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year has not been spent. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said on Wednesday he expected to release findings on the root cause by Friday; the Transportation Department has not issued any findings.

 SubjectiveUnited States Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation — Commerce Committee Democrats Demand Clear & Fact-Based Answers From DOT, FAA on Root Cause of Nov. 13th Nationwide Ground StopAll Democratic members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, led by Ranking Member Senator Maria Cantwell, sent a letter to Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Brian Bedford demanding clear, fact-based answers about the root cause of last Friday’s nationwide ground stop. The Department and the FAA have blamed a router malfunction in Arkansas and FAA contractor L3 Harris’s work converting the FAA’s communications network from copper to fiber for the disruption. The Senators wrote that identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed, that the FAA must investigate further to determine the root cause, and that Congress expects a briefing on improvements before the FAA resumes deployment of the routers. The letter requests an immediate pause on the deployment of additional Juniper devices, and answers by November 23.

 SubjectiveTowerScope — Nationwide FAA ground stop, Nov. 13, 2026: impact and recoveryThe FAA has not published a finding on the cause; the root cause is still under investigation. Senate Commerce Democrats asked the FAA to pause new Juniper routers, and the FAA says it already has: the agency’s questions-and-answers page says it disabled the function on the originating Juniper routers and, as a precaution, on more than 60 other Juniper routers in the system, and has paused installing them. The Democratic senators’ November 16 letter requested a joint technical briefing with the FAA, L3Harris and Juniper, and answers by November 23, on safety assessments, failover, independent validation and rollback procedures. The committee has not yet posted an account of today’s staff briefing in this file. The copper-to-fiber conversion covers 3,648 routers to Juniper devices, of which 400 have been installed and 69 are operational, according to the contractor figures the senators cited.

 SubjectiveHormuz Now — Strait of Hormuz News Today: Latest Status Update (23 Nov 2026)Four crossings today so far: on 23 November 2026, four AIS-visible commercial ships have crossed the Strait of Hormuz—three inbound into the Gulf, one outbound, two of them tankers—as of 21:17 UTC. Yesterday, on 22 November 2026, three commercial ships crossed—two inbound, one outbound, no tankers. In the last seven days, 54 crossings—35 inbound, 19 outbound—including 16 tankers and one LNG or LPG carrier. The most recent crossing detected was the crude oil tanker Ottoman Equity, inbound into the Gulf, at 13:08 UTC on 23 November. Traffic is about 9 percent of normal: 7.7 a day over the past week, against 84.8 before the crisis. The brief is written automatically from AIS-visible counts of commercial ships crossing its counting line, and is not edited.

 SubjectiveStrait of Hormuz Ship Monitor — Ship Directory: Vessels Tracked in the Strait of HormuzIn the 24 hours to 19:01 UTC on 23 November 2026, 28 ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz—17 into the Gulf, 11 out of it—and tankers carried an estimated 2.09 million barrels of oil out through the strait. The monitor tracks every commercial vessel moving between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman from AIS transponder data collected every 30 minutes. Its table for the day lists, among others, crossings in the afternoon hours UTC by small cargo and service vessels in both directions.

 SubjectiveQNC News — Final 40dB Poll Puts PP Ahead of PSOE as Spain Enters Five Day Ban on Polls Before ElectionThe final tracking poll of the Spanish election campaign by 40dB for El Pa&iacute;s and Cadena SER has put the Partido Popular of Alberto N&uacute;&ntilde;ez Feij&oacute;o narrowly ahead of the Socialist Party of Prime Minister Pedro S&aacute;nchez, with the two parties separated by less than one point a week before voting. The poll, based on 2,000 interviews carried out between 18 and 22 November and published on Monday, gives the PP 31.8 percent of the vote and 132 seats in the 350-seat Congress of Deputies, the PSOE 30.9 percent and 122 seats, Vox 17.3 percent and 56 seats, and Frente Amplio 4.4 percent and seven seats. Monday is the last day on which opinion polls may legally be published in Spain before the general election on Sunday 29 November; a five-day ban on new polls now runs until voting ends, and the parties will close their campaigns on Friday before a day of reflection on Saturday.

 SubjectivePollar — Final Spanish polls show right-wing bloc majority before 29NSpanish law bans publishing pre-election polls in the five days before a vote, so media released their final estimates on Monday, 23 November, six days before the general election on Sunday, 29 November. Those surveys give the right-wing bloc a comfortable absolute majority, but the Partido Popular would still need Vox to reach La Moncloa. The GAD3 barometer for ABC projects 194 seats for the PP and Vox bloc, 63 for Vox and 110 for the PSOE. Eldiario.es counts 302 of the 350 seats as certain or probable, leaving 48 in play. On Monday, 23 November, Mr. S&aacute;nchez holds a rally in C&oacute;rdoba, and Mr. Feij&oacute;o gives a morning interview on Antena 3 and answers questions on Telecinco at 21:00. Polls put the PP ahead of the PSOE, and Mr. Feij&oacute;o has asked his supporters not to relax before the vote.

### Nvidia's Board Brings Back Mr. Huang and Wall Street Leaps With Him, Moscow Answers Benghazi With 'Taken Note,' and Dymer's Missing Fall to Two

Filed as: Edition No. 82 — The Midday Watch · 2026-11-23T12:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-23-midday-watch.html

The Midday File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Nvidia’s Board Brings Back Mr. Huang and Wall Street Leaps With Him, Moscow Answers Benghazi With ‘Taken Note,’ and Dymer’s Missing Fall to Two

 The news at midday—corrections to the morning’s counts, the markets’ reading, the official statements: a chief executive restored by unanimous vote and a market that rose on the restoration, a two-word answer from Moscow where the night file carried silence, a missing count cut from eleven to two in Dymer, and a Sunday strait count corrected from two crossings to three.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1200 ET, Monday, November 23, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 81, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, from Edition No. 80, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 79, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Sunday, and from Edition No. 78, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Sunday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midday figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midday in Brief: A Restoration on Wall Street, an Answer From Moscow, and a Missing Count Cut in Dymer

The midday file is a boardroom reversal that moved the whole market, an answer where the night file carried silence, and a search count corrected downward by nine. Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and board director, effective immediately, in the company’s announcement filed below, eleven days after it accepted his resignation and a week after it said on its earnings call that it did not intend to bring him back. By the midday readings the Nasdaq Composite was up 5.9 percent, the S&P 500 up 4.1 percent and the Dow up 2.7 percent, nearly 1,300 points, with Nvidia itself up about a third, in the market account filed below. In Moscow, the Kremlin spokesman answered the Benghazi claim the Overnight Watch had carried unanswered: Russia has “taken note” of President Zelensky’s statement, and the defence ministry is handling it, in the updated claim account filed below. In Dymer, the toll stands at 11 and the fate of two people is still unknown, in the wire account filed below—against the eleven people rescuers were still searching for in the Sunday file. The desk takes the files in that order.

What midday settled is plain: that Mr. Huang is back, by unanimous vote, with the board stating it received input from senior levels of the United States government and is confident his return poses no national security risk; that the cash market held and enlarged the futures bounce the night file had left open; that Moscow has spoken, in two words and a referral; and that Dymer’s unknown are two, not eleven. What it left open is the rest: the board’s continuing investigation, the close at 1600, the defence ministry’s account of Benghazi if it issues one, Dymer’s final count, the North Atlantic Council’s results in Brussels, and the answers on the November 13 ground stop that fall due today in Washington.

The Markets at 1200: Mr. Huang Restored by Unanimous Vote, Nvidia Up a Third, and Anthropic Standing Still in a Rising Market

The announcement came before the opening bell, and the desk prints its operative sentences whole. Effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board; the Board voted unanimously, after a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which it was satisfied with respect to his candor and ability to lead; the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input is confident that his reinstatement poses no national security risk, in the company’s announcement above. Chair Harvey C. Jones: “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.” Colette Kress, who served as interim chief executive, remains chief financial officer, and the independent committee’s investigation into reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort continues, in the same announcement. President Trump, who had urged the return, called it in a Truth Social post “the correct and proper decision,” in the board account filed below. The reversal against the board’s own recent word is in the file and the desk does not smooth it: last week the board said it had unanimously accepted the resignation and did not intend to reinstate Mr. Huang as CEO, in the Journal account filed below.

The market’s reading, at midday, is the largest single-day answer in the file since the sell-off began. Nvidia leapt 33 percent in early trading in one wire reading, 32 percent in another, and 30 percent in a third, on pace to add a record $847.8 billion in market capitalization, in the wire views account and the movers account filed below; the premarket reading had been 29 percent, in the board account. The indexes followed the one stock: the Nasdaq rallied 6 percent and the S&P 500 rose 4 percent in the wire’s rounding, against the market account’s 5.9 and 4.1, with the Dow up 2.7 percent. The chips rose with their maker—Micron up 14 percent, Dell up 17 to 20 percent across readings, Marvell, Intel and others up more than 12 percent, the semiconductor fund up 11 percent and the memory fund up 19 percent, in the market and movers accounts. The one large name that did not rise is the week’s other story: Anthropic stood little changed at around $89 in the market account, and down 0.7 percent in the movers account, after falling 8.5 percent on Friday, its second day of trading—this after rising close to 4 percent in the premarket readings, in the futures account filed below. The futures bounce the Overnight Watch left open at 0400—S&P futures up about 2.2 percent, Nasdaq futures near 3 percent—is therefore answered in the cash market, and enlarged: the question the night posed was whether the bounce would survive the open, and at 1200 it has, on one company’s governance news. Bitcoin traded at $63,800 in the market account’s recent reading, against $61,457 at 0758 UTC in the night file; gold futures were up nearly 4 percent at $3,655 an ounce; WTI oil was down 1.8 percent at $81.95; and the ten-year Treasury yield stood at 4.98 percent, up from 4.94 at Friday’s close, in the same account. Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom report after the close, and the market closes Thursday for Thanksgiving and early on Friday.

The day’s other deal ran against the rally’s grain in its buyer’s stock. CrowdStrike said on Monday it would buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing the company at about $43.9 billion, at 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share—a premium of about 34 percent to Zscaler’s Friday close—expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028, in the deal account filed below. Zscaler gained 17 percent to $228.50 and CrowdStrike dropped 9.8 percent, the worst performer in the S&P 500, in the movers account. Settled: the restoration, and the midday prices. Open: the close, and the investigation the board says continues—Mr. Huang is also scheduled for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, in the probes account filed below.

The Numbers at 1200: Business Activity Eases to 54.6 in the United States While Germany Jumps to 55.0

The morning’s statistics arrived at 0945 and the desk files them under the rally, where they belong in the day’s order of weight. S&P Global’s flash composite purchasing managers’ index for the United States eased to 54.6 in November, a four-month low, from 55.9 in October; manufacturing slipped to 54.5, a three-month low, from 54.9; and services dropped to 54.7, a four-month low, from 56.1, missing the 55.8 expected, in the survey account filed below. The survey period, November 12 to 20, ran through the stock market sell-off, the same account notes; the compiler estimates the readings remain consistent with about 3 percent annualized growth in the fourth quarter, in the readings account filed below. Europe’s flashes ran the other way in its largest economy: Germany’s composite climbed to 55.0 from 53.4, its fastest pace since early 2022, with manufacturing at a 56-month high of 55.0 and services at a 13-month high of 54.0, in the German account filed below. In Britain the composite eased to 52.3 from 52.9 while the manufacturing output index rose to 54.2, a 27-month high, on sales from AI data centre buildouts, in the London account filed below. Settled: the flashes, in their disagreement across the Atlantic. Open: the finals, and Wednesday’s PCE reading.

Libya at 1200: Moscow Has ‘Taken Note,’ the Defence Ministry Holds the File, and a Flag Is Corrected in Malta

The Overnight Watch closed the Benghazi file with Russia not yet commented in any account; midday corrects that line, in the open. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that Russia had “taken note” of President Zelensky’s statement about the attacks: “Our defense ministry is handling this. Any information—should it be deemed necessary to release any—will be provided through the defense ministry,” in the updated claim account above. Of the Baltic attack on the Sparta II, Mr. Peskov said it was “very dangerous” and represents “an escalation of tension in the region,” in the same account. No defence ministry statement on the Merkury stands in the file at the stamp; the ministry had not commented on the loss by the time of the specialist file’s update, in the defence account filed below. Kyiv’s side gained one mechanical particular in the morning: the drone boats were transported to the designated location and launched from a so-called “mothership,” Ukraine’s intelligence agency said, in the claim account, and the Security Service of Ukraine said the seven uncrewed vessels reached their targets despite attempts to destroy them from the air, sea and land, in the defence account. The second ship’s name held in Kyiv’s word—the MV Angara, named by the Security Service with her IMO number as a roll-on/roll-off cargo ship, in the defence account—and one flag in the file was corrected: Malta’s Minister for Home Affairs and Security, Glenn Bedingfield, said the Ascalon was not flying the Maltese flag, contrary to reports in some international media, in the same account. The eastern government’s joint investigation with Russia and its letter to the United Nations stand as filed; Tripoli’s government said it was following the reports with “grave concern” about exposing civilian ports to external conflict, in the Journal account filed below. Settled: Moscow has answered, and its answer is a referral. Open: the ministry’s account, if it comes.

Dymer at 1200: Eleven Dead, Two Still Unknown, and at Least Fifteen Dead Across the Kyiv Region

Dymer’s midday figures correct the night’s open end downward and the region’s toll upward, and the desk prints both movements. The building’s toll stands at 11, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko’s Monday figure, unmoved since the morning; the youngest of those killed was 11 years old, the Kyiv regional prosecutor’s office said, in the wire account above. The fate of two people is still unknown, President Zelenskiy said on Monday—against the eleven people, including two children, whom the emergency service said on Sunday rescuers were still searching for as unresponsive or unreachable, in the regional account filed below. The police figure in another account agrees with the president’s: two people still missing and seven injured, including two children, regional police said on Monday morning, in the Dymer account filed below. The two survivors stand as the night filed them—Davyd, seven, treated in hospital with his parents beside him, and Valentyna, seventy-nine, pulled alive at 0328 after twenty-two hours—with four other injured people also in hospital, in the wire account. Search operations had to be halted several times because of the threat of further attacks and the danger from Shahed drones, Mr. Zelenskiy said, in the same account. The wider count moved the other way: the strikes on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people, in the regional account’s agency file, of whom Dymer’s building accounts for 11. The Kyiv region declared Monday a day of mourning, in the Dymer account. Settled: eleven in the building, two unknown, at least fifteen in the region. Open: the two, and the final count when the search ends.

Brussels and Washington at 1200: A Council in Session With No Communique Expected, and Answers Due on the Ground Stop

The North Atlantic Council’s extraordinary meeting on the three Kh-101 missiles Poland’s prosecutors confirmed on Sunday stands in the midday file as convening and in session, not concluded. The particulars the room works from gained one detail in the prosecutors’ account: the missiles were manufactured in the fourth quarter of 2026 at facilities in Dubna, in the Moscow district, in the confirmation account filed below. Poland has not formally triggered the treaty’s Article 4 consultation mechanism; Warsaw instead requested additional NATO assets and allied consultations, and no joint communique is expected from Monday’s meeting, with Secretary General Rutte expected to present the results after the talks, in the meeting account filed below. At the stamp no readout stands in the file; the Evening Watch will file what the room produces.

Washington’s dated business for the day is an answer that has not yet appeared in print. The Senate Commerce Committee Democrats’ letter of November 16 asked the Department of Transportation and the Federal Aviation Administration for answers by November 23 on the November 13 nationwide ground stop—on safety assessments, failover, independent validation and rollback procedures for the Juniper routers at the centre of the failure—and for a pause on further deployment, in the committee account filed below. The standing public record at midday is the agency’s own: the broadcasting function disabled on the originating routers and, as a precaution, on more than 60 others, installations paused, and the root cause still under investigation, with no finding published, in the ground-stop file filed below, which records no account of today’s answers yet posted. The conversion at issue covers 3,648 routers, of which 400 have been installed and 69 are operational, on the contractor figures the senators cited. Settled: the deadline is today. Open: the answers.

The Strait and Spain at 1200: One Crossing by Midday, Sunday Corrected to Three, and the Polls Gone Dark

The strait’s visible counter carries one crossing for Monday at the stamp—the oil products tanker Musik, inbound at 0437 UTC, one inbound and none outbound—and it corrects its own Sunday in the same brief: three crossings on Sunday, two inbound and one outbound, no tankers, against the two the counter’s earlier readings had closed the day at, in the strait count filed below. The seven-day figure stands at 51 crossings in that brief, 33 inbound and 18 outbound, 15 of them tankers, about 9 percent of the pre-crisis 84.8 a day. The second instrument counts its wider sea for the 24 hours to 1331 UTC: 27 ships, 17 in and 10 out, with tankers carrying an estimated 0.00 million barrels out, and its table again lists the tanker the desk struck from the record on Sunday as a spoof transmission, not restored on the monitor’s word, in the monitor account filed below. Settled: Monday’s first crossing, and Sunday’s corrected three. Open: the week’s true figure, on which the two instruments still do not agree.

Spain’s campaign passed its last polling day at the stamp. The final 40dB poll, from 2,000 interviews taken November 18 to 22 and published Monday, gives the People’s Party 31.8 percent and 132 seats, the Socialists 30.9 and 122, Vox 17.3 and 56, and Frente Amplio 4.4 and seven, in the final poll account filed below; the wider final surveys give the two parties of the right a combined majority—GAD3 projects 194 seats for the bloc—with 48 of the 350 seats counted in play, in the final polls account filed below. Monday is the last day polls may legally be published; the five-day ban now runs until voting ends on November 29, the campaigns close Friday, and Saturday is the day of reflection. Mr. S&aacute;nchez campaigns in C&oacute;rdoba today and Mr. Feij&oacute;o appears on television tonight, in the final polls account. Settled: the last numbers, in their disagreement. Open: the vote itself, six days out, with no new poll permitted to move it in print.

The Cocked Hat

Where the midday bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On Nvidia’s rise: up 33 percent in early trading in the wire’s reading, 32 percent in the movers account, 30 percent in the market account, and 29 percent in premarket trading in the board account—four readings of one ascent, taken at four hours. On Anthropic: up 4.8 percent premarket in the wire futures account and close to 4 percent in another, little changed at around $89 in the market account, and down 0.7 percent in the movers account. On Bitcoin: $61,457 at 0758 UTC in the night file, around $61,500 in the morning futures reading, and $63,800 in the market account’s recent reading. On Dymer’s unknown: two people, in the president’s Monday word and the regional police’s; eleven people, including two children, in the emergency service’s Sunday figure carried in the regional account. On Dymer’s dead: eleven in the building, in the governor’s word; at least fifteen across the Kyiv region, in the agency file. On Sunday in the strait: three crossings, in the counter’s corrected brief; two, in the readings the night file closed on. On the strait’s day: one crossing in the visible counter; twenty-seven ships in twenty-four hours in the monitor’s wider count. On Spain’s right: 188 seats on the final 40dB figures and 194 in the GAD3 projection. Inside the triangle is where midday honestly stands, and the log turns on it. The Evening Watch collects at 1800.

 The Clippings Filed With This Edition

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 34 items.

 
 SubjectiveNVIDIA — Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board DirectorNVIDIA announced on November 23, 2026 that, effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with him, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to his candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. Board Chair Harvey C. Jones said the Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of stockholders, employees, partners and customers, and thanked Colette Kress for her service as interim CEO alongside her continuing responsibilities as Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Huang said he was honored to return and took the responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.
